verdict.rationale: npm's own docs show `npm install` and `npm install <pkg>` as the core dependency-install commands, configurable through `NPM_CONFIG_` environment variables and `--key val` switches, which supports scripted, agent-driven use. Nothing in the pack documents exit codes, error formats, a non-interactive guarantee or an update command. One community comment says differing min-release-age units make LLM agents spin on install failures, which suggests failure signals are not always clear to agents. missing for 10: documented exit codes and error semantics, an explicit non-interactive/CI mode, documentation of the update command, independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven installs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent install and update project dependencies non-interactively, with clear exit codes and errors when something fails

citations.quote: The very first thing you will most likely want to run in any node program is `npm install` to install its dependencies.
You can also run `npm install blerg` to install the latest version of "blerg".
Set any config by prefixing the name in an environment variable with `NPM_CONFIG_`.
Command line switches: Set a config with `--key val`.
